# ST VD55G0 Linux driver

## Installation

### Driver

Compile the driver using the Makefile

```
make
```

Place it in the kernel modules folder.

```
sudo cp vd55g0.ko /lib/modules/$(uname -r)
```

Resolve modules dependencies.

```
sudo depmod -a
```

### Device tree

Compile the device tree overlay matching your platform and plugin board from the `dts` folder.

```
sudo dtc <device-tree>.dts -o /boot/firmware/overlays/<device-tree>.dtbo
```

Set the device tree overlay in your platform. This may differ from platform to platform. Please refer to your platform documentation.

Microsoft Surface touch/pen data parser
=======================================

`surface-parser.py` parses MS Surface multitouch/pen data and prints it in a human-readable format.

You must specify one or more data files to parse. Files can be gzipped. It is possible to read from `/dev/hidraw*` directly.

You must specify the input format using one of the following options:
- `--hidraw`: Data read directly from `/dev/hidraw*` device.
- `--ithc`: Data captured from legacy `/dev/ithc` device.

This directory contains an out-of-tree Linux driver patch for the ambient-light
and proximity sensor exposed as ACPI device `MSHW0184` on Microsoft Surface
Laptop 5 systems.

On the tested Surface Laptop 5, ACPI maps the APDS9960-compatible sensor to an
IRQ that the Tiger Lake pin controller refuses to use:

```text
tigerlake-pinctrl INTC1055:00: pin 99 cannot be used as IRQ
```

The upstream `apds9960` driver treats failure to request that IRQ as a fatal
probe error. This patch uses polling mode on Surface Laptop 5
